name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with an 11-point partisan lean
Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Kennedy at roughly 96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Kennedy: an 11-point Democratic lean, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and a roughly $2.3 million warchest against a little-known, underfunded challenger. Markets agree, pricing Kennedy near 96%, so the forecast stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Hannon or an unexpectedly hostile national environment could narrow the margin, though an upset would still require a major shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent in this Buffalo-area district, seeks another term after winning the seat in a 2024 special election. The district leans Democratic by about 11 points, and Kennedy enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised over $2.3 million and holding more than $1.2 million on hand. Republican Dennis Hannon has reported no significant fundraising and lacks outside support.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Kennedy's chances at roughly 96 percent. The combination of incumbency, a strong partisan lean, and a favorable environment makes this a safely Democratic seat, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
